16.5.7.8 Polymerization

Polymerization is a process in which small molecules (monomers) chemically join together to form large molecules (polymers). Simple alkenes when subjected to high temperature and pressure in the presence of a catalyst, form long chain addition polymers. Polymerization of alkenes is essentially the conversion of pi bonds to sigma bonds, which is a thermodynamically favorable process. For example ethene polymerizes to form polyethene in different ways. One approach involves relatively high pressure (2000 atm) and high temperature (200 °C) and the use of a free radical initiator catalyst such as peroxides.

Polyethylene is used as plastic material in the industries. It is used in the manufacture of shopping bags, sport nets, dustbins, water pipes, packing materials and cable insulation.

16.6 Isomerism

Many of the organic compounds have the same molecular formula but they are different from each other in their structure and properties. Such compounds are called isomers and this phenomenon is called isomerism.

Tidbit

There are two main types of isomerism i.e. Constitutional or Structural isomerism and Stereoisomerism. Each of these two main types of isomerism is further classified into different types as shown in Figure 16.5.

In this type of isomerism, the isomers have the same molecular formula but different connectivity in structure. It is also called structural isomerism. Structural isomerism is of five types.

د iso- مختاړی له یوناني isos ټکي څخه اخیستل شوی چې «یو شان» معنا لري. په «isomer» ټکي کې د –mer وروستاړی له یوناني meros څخه اخیستل شوی چې «برخه» معنا لري. نو ایزومرونه بېلابېل مالیکولونه دي چې یو شان برخې (عنصري ترکیب) لري.

د ایزومېریزم دوه اصلي ډولونه شته، یعنې کانسټیټیوشنل یا جوړښتي ایزومېریزم او سټیریوایزومېریزم. له دې دوو اصلي ډولونو څخه هر یو بیا په بېلابېلو ډولونو وېشل کېږي، لکه په شکل16.5 کې چې ښودل شوي.

شکل16.5 د ایزومېریزم بېلابېل ډولونه.

16.6.1 جوړښتي ایزومېریزم

د ایزومېریزم په دې ډول کې ایزومرونه یو شان مالیکولي فورمول لري، خو په جوړښت کې یې د اټومونو نښلېدنه توپیر لري. دې ته جوړښتي ایزومېریزم هم ویل کېږي. جوړښتي ایزومېریزم پنځه ډولونه لري.

16.6.1.1 ځنځیري ایزومېریزم یا سکلیټي ایزومېریزم

ځنځیري ایزومېریزم هغه وخت رامنځته کېږي چې د یوه مالیکول په اصلي ځنځیر کې د کاربني اټومونو په ترتیب کې توپیر وي. که دوه یا ډېر مرکبات یو شان مالیکولي فورمول خو بېلابېل کاربني ځنځیرونه ولري، ویل کېږي چې هغوی د ځنځیري ایزومېریزم ځانګړنه ښيي. دې پدیدې ته سکلیټي ایزومېریزم هم ویل کېږي. د ممکنه ځنځیري ایزومرونو شمېر د کاربني اټومونو له شمېر سره زیاتېږي. د بېلګې په توګه، بیوټان دوه ایزومرونه، پینټان درې، هېکسان پنځه ایزومرونه لري او داسې نور. د بیوټان (C₄H₁₀) دوه ځنځیري ایزومرونه لاندې ورکړل شوي دي.

16.6.1.2 موقعیتي ایزومېریزم

موقعیتي ایزومېریزم هغه وخت رامنځته کېږي چې د فعالي ګروپ په موقعیت کې توپیر وي. کله چې د اصلي ځنځیر په نسبت د فعالي ګروپونو موقعیت بدل شي، دې پدیدې ته موقعیتي ایزومېریزم ویل کېږي. د بېلګې په توګه، د پروپیل الکولونو او بیوټیلینونو موقعیتي ایزومرونه لاندې ورکړل شوي دي.

Ozonides are highly unstable and explosive and cannot be isolated. Ozonides are decomposed using reducing agents like zinc dust, to form carbonyl compounds. For example, cleavage of ethylene ozonide with zinc, yield two molecules of formaldehyde.

This conversion process of an alkene using ozone to carbonyl compounds is called ozonolysis. This reaction can be used for locating the position of the double bond in an unknown alkene.

16.5.7.8 Polymerization

Polymerization is a process in which small molecules (monomers) chemically join together to form large molecules (polymers). Simple alkenes when subjected to high temperature and pressure in the presence of a catalyst, form long chain addition polymers. Polymerization of alkenes is essentially the conversion of pi bonds to sigma bonds, which is a thermodynamically favorable process. For example ethene polymerizes to form polyethene in different ways. One approach involves relatively high pressure (2000 atm) and high temperature (200 °C) and the use of a free radical initiator catalyst such as peroxides.

Polyethylene is used as plastic material in the industries. It is used in the manufacture of shopping bags, sport nets, dustbins, water pipes, packing materials and cable insulation.

16.6 Isomerism

Many of the organic compounds have the same molecular formula but they are different from each other in their structure and properties. Such compounds are called isomers and this phenomenon is called isomerism.

Tidbit

The prefix iso- is derived from Greek word isos, “the same”. The suffix –mer in the word “isomer” is derived from the Greek word meros, meaning “part”. Thus isomers are different molecules that have the same parts (elemental composition).

There are two main types of isomerism i.e. Constitutional or Structural isomerism and Stereoisomerism. Each of these two main types of isomerism is further classified into different types as shown in Figure 16.5.

Figure 16.5 Different types of isomerism.

16.6.1 Constitutional isomerism

In this type of isomerism, the isomers have the same molecular formula but different connectivity in structure. It is also called structural isomerism. Structural isomerism is of five types.

16.6.1.1 Chain Isomerism or Skeletal Isomerism

Chain isomerism occurs when there is a difference in arrangement of the carbon atoms in main chain of a molecule. If two or more compounds having the same molecular formula with different carbon chains, then they are said to exhibit the property of Chain isomerism. This phenomenon is also called as skeletal isomerism. The number of possible chain isomers increases with number of carbon atoms. For example; butane has two isomers, pentane has three, hexane has five isomers and so on. The two chain isomers of butane (C₄H₁₀) are given below.

16.6.1.2 Position Isomerism

Position isomerism arises when there is a difference in the position of functional group. When the position of the functional groups with respect to main chain changes, the phenomenon is called as position isomerism. For example; position isomers of propyl alcohols and butylenes are given below.
